open.fact: CR-1457 does not tabulate specimen knockdown, R/t, Vc or imperfection amplitude for the two retained hemisphere points. They are on figure 6.2-3. The figure was not digitized. OCR of the page was not usable. Coordinates were not invented.
The test Vc of those two hemispheres is not in the prose. The design branch Vc<2 covers 0.9 to 1.1. That is not a measurement that the specimens sat in that band.
No published external-pressure test of a closed sphere with a bonded beryllium face on CR-III honeycomb was found. The admissible value remains the aluminum / glass-fabric hemisphere floor.
Ribbon direction and cure of the 1964 specimens are not in the CR-1457 prose. The product form is aluminum face on glass-fabric honeycomb, not beryllium on CR-III.
Two retained domes carried a thermal gradient, inner face about +280 F and outer face about +10 F, which the reduction ignored.
Gonzalez and Patton, SDL 468, May 1964, was not fetched. The specimen table may live there. This card used CR-1457's own account of that report.
The monocoque floor near 0.14 is from secondary reviews of NASA SP-8032. The primary was not opened. It is tagged QUESTIONABLE and is not the design gamma.
10.2514/3.5568 and 10.2514/3.1932 are not external-pressure tests of a sphere or a sandwich dome. Cited by DOI only. They supply no gamma.

At Q 0.33 the optima leave Vc 0.9 to 1.1 and sit at Vc 1.60 to 1.64. Gamma remains 0.20 because Vc stays below 2. Face wrinkling binds. Those four cells are outside the admissibility scenario even though the handbook step is unchanged.

T7 still has to be a closed sandwich shell in this product form, at Vc 0.9 to 1.1, under external pressure, in the elastic range, with imperfection amplitude, ribbon direction and cure recorded. It has to show whether gamma can stand above 0.20. Until that measurement P2 carries 0.20. Purchase of the surrogate is not this card's act.
The model is a PROJECTION on QUESTIONABLE inherited inputs. qualified_hull_SF is null. Closure density is the factor that zeros concept payload. It is not an installed safety factor.

Whether any sourced isotropic sheet reaches about 1238 kg/m3 at about 294 GPa was not re-opened. 017b's card said no. That is a pointer, not a new finding, and those older gamma factors are a different model.

simjob-20261020t170724-7b19e90142a9 exited 1 because the driver rejected Vc outside 0.9 to 1.1. The model had already matched the Q 0.33 concept payload. The record is simjob-20261020t170832-d919922bc1af, exit 0.
